what: The counted Runs of the step 1 circuit experiment, the positive control of the breeder with the simulated designer (docs/PREREG_STEP1_CIRCUITS.md). It says nothing about real language models.

tests.cargo test --test circuits: ok. 18 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
tests.cargo test --example circuit_positive_co: ok. 31 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

binary: cargo build --release --bin brut-breed at the frozen commit
threads: RAYON_NUM_THREADS unset for the counted Runs (rayon's default, one thread per CPU); 1 and 4 for the thread check

stop.why: the primary claim is proven and E2 has crossed a threshold

primary.claim: ticket 03: more than half of all seeds pass within 1000 generations (rejects the pass rate <= 1/2)

secondary.claim: selection: among untied pairs, arm A passes first more often than arm R (rejects P(A first | not tied) <= 1/2)

error_bound: each claim is made falsely with probability at most 1/100, and some claim is made falsely with probability at most 1/100 (Ville's inequality and the fixed sequence of the two claims)

checks.thread_check: 2026-10-30T23:18:57Z thread check ok: five files byte-equal at the default, 1 and 4 threads, both arms

notes: Every number below is recomputed by make_counted.py from the files of the Runs and the logs of the driver; the script stops with an error if one differs from analysis.txt, recount.txt or hashes.txt. Floats are rounded to 4 decimal places.
frozen_commit: the commit at which the driver ran, from its 'driver started at commit' lines; it is the squash merge of PR #19, at which docs/PREREG_STEP1_CIRCUITS.md is frozen.
toolchain and tests: from step1-build-test.txt, the build and the three test commands of PREREG section 6 step 1 at the frozen commit.

threads: the driver set no RAYON_NUM_THREADS for the counted Runs, so rayon used one thread per CPU; the thread check found the files of seed 1 byte-equal at the default, 1 and 4 threads (thread_check); the wall time depends on the thread count.
stop: the pair after which the rule of PREREG section 8 stopped, and which of its three stop rules applied.
verdicts: each claim with the pair at which its evidence value first crossed a threshold, and its evidence value at the stop, as a fraction and as a decimal.
error_bound: PREREG section 8; it holds however the experiment stops, under the conduct and the assumptions stated there.
descriptive: results with no decision attached (PREREG section 8): the median of D_A, the T-only variant, the Runs that ended at the call cap and the invention candidates.

checks: what the script checked; hash_lines counts the lines of hashes.txt, distinct_hash_lines its distinct lines. Pair 1's ten lines appear twice, because the driver, started again after the container restart, verified pair 1 again and appended its hashes again; both copies are equal.
pairs: one entry per counted pair, in the order of the seed list (PREREG section 8, 'Reported per pair').
pairs.r_seed: the targets the seed Cascades solve; it is the same in both arms.
pairs.d_a, pairs.d_r: D of the arm A and the arm R Run at generation 1000, as hits/open where open = |L \ R_seed| (not reduced, as the analysis prints it).
pairs.t_a, pairs.t_r: the pass times T (PREREG section 7), the first generation with 2 * |R_bred(<= g) \ R_seed| > |L \ R_seed|; null means never by generation 1000.
pairs.x: 1 when the arm A Run passes (T_A <= 1000), else 0.
pairs.y: 'A first' when T_A < T_R, 'R first' when T_R < T_A, 'tie' when they are equal, including when neither Run passes; never counts as later than every generation.
pairs.e1, pairs.e2: the evidence values after the pair, E1 = 3^passes / 2^pairs and E2 = 3^(A first) / 2^(untied pairs), as fractions; e1_value and e2_value are decimals.
pairs.primary, pairs.secondary: 'open', 'proven' or 'failed' after the pair, by the integer tests 3^k >= 100 * 2^n (proven) and 20 * 3^k <= 2^n (failed); a verdict is final at its first crossing.
pairs.d_a_t_only, pairs.d_r_t_only: D under the T-only variant (descriptive): a target counts when the cheapest exact answer has T <= T_ref, and also CNOT <= CNOT_ref where T_ref = 0.
runs: one entry per counted Run, in the order A-1, R-1, A-2, R-2, ...
runs.generations, runs.max_calls: --generations and --max-calls from config.json.
runs.generations_completed counts generation 0 (the seed Cascades) and the bred generations 1 to 1000.
runs.stop_reason, runs.calls_used, runs.archive_size, runs.comparisons: from report.json; calls_used counts every Worker call of the Run, the select phase included.
runs.calls_by_generation_1000: calls_used of the generation event of generation 1000 in events.jsonl, before the select phase; PREREG section 6 bounds it by 12 723 412.
runs.wall_seconds: wall time of the Run's process, the seconds between its last 'start' line and its 'done' line in driver.log (1 s resolution, one process at a time); minutes is the same in minutes.

runs.attempts: how many times the driver started the Run; interrupted_attempt gives the start of an attempt that never finished and the time the driver removed it (PREREG section 6 step 3; deviation 1).

runs.library: |L|; r_seed, r_bred: the targets the seed and the bred Cascades solve (PREREG section 7); r_bred_only: R_bred \ R_seed; d: D as hits/open; d_value: D as a decimal; calibrated: the gate 3 * |R_seed| <= |L|; d_above_half: D > 1/2.
runs.pass_time: T of the Run, null for never.
runs.r_seed_t_only, runs.d_t_only: R_seed and D under the T-only variant.

runs.targets: per target of L, in library order: reference, best_seed and best_bred are [T, CNOT] of the library reference and of the cheapest exact answer of the seed and of the bred Cascades (null when none was exact); seed_hit: the seed Cascades solve it; first_bred_generation: the earliest generation of a bred member that solved one of the target's dressed search tasks (null when none did); calls_to_first_hit: calls_used of the generation event of that generation, the calls through it (descriptive).
runs.invention_candidates: targets with an exact answer below a BestKnown count (below_best_known or candidate in rediscovery.json).

runs.integrity_alarm: false when the Run finished with exit code 0 and wrote rediscovery.json; a Run with an alarm exits with code 1 and has no rediscovery.json, and the driver stops at any other exit code (step1-driver.sh).

runs.verify: events is the number of events in events.jsonl and head the hash of its last event, the head that brut-breed --verify reports; chain_linked: every event's prev equals the hash of the event before it (the script does not recompute the hashes; --verify does). logged: the times of the driver's 'verify ok' lines; the driver writes one only when the last line of --verify contains 'report recomputed and equal; rediscovery recomputed and equal', which brut-breed prints at the end of that line (PREREG section 6 step 4; step1-driver.sh).
runs.sha256: the SHA-256 of the five files that hashes.txt records; each equals its line there.

runs.best_single_cascade_solved: the most search tasks one member of the archive solves, the largest 'solved' of the born events; best_by_fitness_solved: 'solved' of the best member by fitness (report.json, top[0]); they need not be the same Cascade (descriptive).
runs.select: select-panel hits of the finalists and of the seed Cascades, select_solved of the 22 select tasks (report.json, finalists), and the best rates (descriptive).
runs.trajectory: the state line of every 10th generation, one row per line in the order of trajectory_columns (descriptive).
thread_check: PREREG section 6 step 5, from driver.log: seed 1 of each arm again at RAYON_NUM_THREADS 1 and 4, with the wall time and the time of the driver's 'verify ok' line of each Run.
deviations: the deviations from the pre-registration, with deviations.txt as the source.
